problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=6 \\ 2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=12 \\ -2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{3}=12\end{aligned}
$$

activity_context.topic_title: The Least-Squares Solution of a Linear System (Without Collinearity)

feedback.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=18 \\ {x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=18 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}18 \\ 0 \\ 18 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}}\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}18 \\ 0 \\ 18 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 18 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}36 \\ 72 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{36}[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 18\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}36 \\ 72 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
